title: Successor step for the tabulation invariant
statement: Let $\kappa$ be a finite set of instruction kinds, let $m,w,n$ be nonnegative integers, let $F$ assign to each kind a function from Boolean lists to Boolean lists, let $z$ be a Boolean list, and let $x$ be an assignment of $n$ Boolean inputs. Suppose every source in each program instruction is valid relative to the inputs formed by adjoining $z$ to the $n$ input bits, with output width $w$, and every instruction has exactly $m$ sources. If $i$ is a position in the program and a list of Boolean vertex values satisfies the tabulation invariant after the first $i$ instructions, then running the gates for instruction $i$ on that list produces vertex values satisfying the invariant after the first $i+1$ instructions.
hypotheses_covered: $F$ maps each instruction kind and Boolean list to a Boolean list
$x$ is an assignment of $n$ Boolean inputs
all program sources are valid relative to $z$ followed by the $n$ inputs, width $w$, and instruction positions
$i$ is less than the program length
the vertex-value list satisfies the tabulation invariant at position $i$
